faqs.question: How do I turn a PES embroidery file into a picture?
faqs.answer: Open it in Inkscape with Ink/Stitch using File > Open and export with Shift+Ctrl+E. If you prefer code, the pyembroidery Python library reads the PES and writes a PNG.

faqs.question: Can I open a PES file without Brother's software?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ink/Stitch costs nothing and lets Inkscape open PES, and it can export PES again.

faqs.question: Is there a phone app that opens PES files?

faqs.question: Will the PNG still sew on my machine?
faqs.answer: No, because a PNG has no stitch coordinates in it. The machine needs the PES.

faqs.question: Does a PES file contain a preview image?
faqs.answer: Yes, the format stores a design preview next to the stitch data and thread colors. This page can't open the file to show it.

faqs.question: Can I choose the size of the PNG?
faqs.answer: Yes. Inkscape's export dialog takes the size of the image in pixels, or a resolution, and updates the other values to match.

faqs.question: Can I change a PES and save it as a PES again?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ink/Stitch opens the file in Manual Stitch Mode, where individual points can be edited, and File > Save a copy... writes a format your machine can read.

guide.title: PES to PNG: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a PES file?

Brother created PES for its embroidery machines, and Babylock machines use it too. Inside are the stitch coordinates, the thread colors and a small preview of the design. That is a sewing recipe for a machine, not a grid of pixels. In the full edition of Brother's PE-DESIGN 11, PES designs also appear as thumbnails in Explorer.

### Programs that open PES files

- **Windows:** PE-DESIGN 11, Brother's own application (its trial limits some features).
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Ink/Stitch, a free extension for Inkscape that imports and exports PES.
- **iOS and Android:** Artspira, Brother's own app, takes PES files.

### PES and PNG compared

A PNG is a raster picture, losslessly compressed, with optional transparency, and every major browser shows it. To get from PES to PNG, a program has to draw the stitches as an image. A sewing machine can't use that picture, so hold on to the PES.

Nothing on this page can draw it. Files are opened by your browser's built-in image decoder, and it has no idea what embroidery data is. Choosing a PES ends in the message "Image decode failed." and no PNG appears. The programs below do the job.

### Other ways to convert PES to PNG

- **Ink/Stitch and Inkscape:** use File > Open on the PES; it opens in Manual Stitch Mode. Then press Shift+Ctrl+E to open the Export PNG Image dialog, export the page, all drawn objects, the selected objects or a custom area, then enter the size in pixels, name the file and click Export.
- **pyembroidery:** in this Python library, `pyembroidery.write_png(pyembroidery.read_pes("design.pes"), "design.png")` reads the PES and writes the PNG. PNG is write-only there.

### Problems with PES files

- **Image decode failed:** that is the browser telling you PES isn't a picture format. Use an embroidery program.
- **The machine can't hold the design:** big designs can overflow a machine's USB storage; Brother recommends a USB flash drive where the machine supports one.
- **Large files:** Brother's support page says PE-DESIGN 11 puts more design information into a PES, which can make the file bigger.
- **More than 255 color changes:** Ink/Stitch's FAQ says a PES file can't save more.

guide.title: PES to SVG: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a PES file?

The PES format comes from Brother and also runs on Babylock machines. Its payload is a list of stitch positions, a thread color palette and a preview of the design. A machine follows the stitches. The artwork a digitizer drew them from is something else entirely, so if you still have that project, keep it.

### Programs that open PES files

- **Windows:** Brother's PE-DESIGN 11, which has a trial with fewer features.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Ink/Stitch, a free Inkscape extension that imports and exports PES.
- **iOS and Android:** the Artspira app accepts PES uploads.

### PES and SVG compared

SVG is an XML language for graphics. It describes shapes, text and embedded images, its shapes stay sharp at any size, and every major browser displays it. A PES, by contrast, lists stitches and thread colors.

This page can't produce either kind of result. A PES goes to your browser's image decoder, which doesn't read embroidery, and ends with "Image decode failed." Even for pictures it does read, the SVG written here wraps one embedded PNG at the picture's pixel size; nothing is traced into vector shapes. For a drawing of the stitches, turn to the programs below.

### Other ways to convert PES to SVG

- **Ink/Stitch and Inkscape:** File > Open brings the PES in as Manual Stitch Mode. When you save, choose Inkscape SVG to keep all the editing data, or Plain SVG when you are sharing the drawing.
- **pyembroidery:** with this Python library, `pyembroidery.write_svg(pyembroidery.read_pes("design.pes"), "design.svg")` reads the PES and writes the SVG. SVG is write-only there.

### Problems with PES files

- **Image decode failed:** your browser read the PES as a picture and couldn't. An embroidery program is the right tool.
- **Color changes over 255:** the Ink/Stitch FAQ says Brother's PES and PEC files can't store them.
- **The design is too big for the machine:** USB storage on a machine can run out, and Brother points to a USB flash drive where one is supported.
- **Bigger files from PE-DESIGN 11:** Brother's support page says the program writes more design information into a PES, so the file can grow.

faqs.question: Can I convert several PNGs at once?

faqs.question: Does the PNG metadata come along?
faqs.answer: No. The pixels pass through on their own, which leaves behind EXIF, ICC profiles and XMP.

faqs.question: What if my PNG is 16-bit?
faqs.answer: Extra depth is discarded, because the pixels pass through at 8 bits per channel. GIMP also insists on an 8-bit image before it offers XBM export.

guide.title: PNG to XBM: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a PNG file?

Developers designed PNG to replace GIF without the patent worries. It reached W3C Recommendation status in October 1996, the first format to do so, and ISO/IEC 15948 came later. Pixels are always stored losslessly. Color can come from a palette, gray levels or full truecolor, and an alpha channel is available for see-through areas. Every major browser shows PNG, and macOS takes screenshots in this format by default.

### Programs that open PNG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP imports PNG for editing.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads PNG.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays PNG.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays PNG.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays PNG.

### PNG and XBM compared

An XBM keeps its picture as C source text, not as a binary image. It served the X graphical environment for icons and pointer artwork, and it may include coordinates for a pointer hot spot. Its image is monochrome, so the colors, grays and transparency of a PNG have nowhere to go and color artwork turns monochrome.

On this page your browser decodes the PNG, and ImageMagick then writes the XBM from those pixels. Metadata is dropped along the way.

### Other ways to convert PNG to XBM

- **GIMP:** open the PNG, choose File > Export As, type a name that ends in .xbm and click Export. GIMP offers XBM only for an image with 8 bits per channel. The export options are an X10 format bitmap, an identifier prefix, a comment, hot spot values, and a mask file that is enabled only when the image has an alpha channel.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick picture.png picture.xbm`. ImageMagick reads and writes XBM, for black and white only.
- **ImageMagick, flattened first:** run `magick picture.png -background white -alpha remove -alpha off -monochrome picture.xbm`. Here `-alpha remove` composites the image over the background color, `-alpha off` disables the alpha channel and `-monochrome` transforms the image to black and white.

### Problems with PNG files

- **Compression setting:** pixels come through exactly as saved, because PNG never discards image data.
- **Layer offsets:** the offset option in GIMP's PNG export places layers in a way other programs may not match, so leave it unchecked.
- **Camera tags and profiles:** an export from GIMP carries them only if you enable its metadata controls.

guide.title: RA to MP3: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is an RA file?

RealAudio is an audio format from RealNetworks, introduced in 1995 for streaming over the internet, and it carried online sound delivery from the mid-1990s onward. The .ra ending can identify audio delivered through RealMedia. The format is proprietary, with limited public technical documentation. The family spans several coding systems, so the extension alone doesn't tell you which codec a file uses. A RealAudio file can hold descriptive information such as a title or artist.

### Programs that open RA files

- **Windows:** RealPlayer, the free PC player, lists RA and RealAudio Lossless among its supported audio types.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg reads RealMedia through its demuxers, though it is a command-line converter and not a graphical player.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay, a portable player built on FFmpeg libraries.

### RA and MP3 compared

The MP3 format dates to the late 1980s work at Fraunhofer IIS with fellow MPEG audio group members, and ISO/IEC 11172-3 standardized it in 1993. A model of human hearing decides which sound it throws away. Every major browser plays MP3, and ID3 structures inside the file store titles and further tags. RealAudio is lossy already, so an MP3 made from it adds one more generation of loss.

On this page FFmpeg runs in your browser and encodes with libmp3lame, asking for 192 kbit/s and leaving video out. Below 32 kHz that rate is out of reach for MP3, so audio sampled low gets a lower bitrate.

### Other ways to convert RA to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.ra -vn -b:a 192k -c:a libmp3lame listening.mp3`.
- **Switch Sound File Converter:** Switch converts from ra and to mp3. Click Add and choose the RA file, type mp3 into the Output Format field and click Convert.

### Problems with RA files

- **The file is just a link:** a .ram companion is a streaming metafile and is not interchangeable with the sound file itself. Look for the .ra it points to.
- **Some RA files play and others don't:** playback needs a decoder for the particular RealAudio variant, because the family includes several different coding systems.
- **Empty tags:** a RealAudio file only has a title or artist if one was stored in it, so otherwise the MP3 has nothing to copy.

guide.title: SVG to TGA: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

An SVG file lists shapes, text and embedded images in XML, and a renderer draws them: that is the Scalable Vector Graphics standard from the W3C. Since the shapes are instructions rather than pixels, the drawing keeps clean edges at whatever size you ask for. The file is text, CSS and JavaScript can act on it, and all major browsers show it. A pixel image embedded in an SVG is the exception, because it keeps its original resolution when enlarged.

### Programs that open SVG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Inkscape, for native SVG editing.
- **Windows, Mac, Linux and Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays SVG.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays SVG.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays SVG.

### SVG and TGA compared

Targa, a raster format tied to Truevision's video boards, keeps turning up in video editing and in game development. It supports RGB, indexed-color and grayscale images. In a 24-bit file every color component gets eight bits; a 32-bit file adds an eight-bit alpha channel. Run-length encoding is optional. Moving from SVG to TGA locks the drawing to a single pixel size, so it can't be scaled up cleanly or edited as shapes again.

Your browser paints the SVG at its reported dimensions; ImageMagick then writes the TGA from those pixels. Metadata doesn't come along. The browser loads nothing from outside the file, so the TGA shows only what the SVG embeds, plus fonts installed on the device.

### Other ways to convert SVG to TGA

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -density 144 artwork.svg artwork.tga`. -density controls the resolution at which ImageMagick draws the SVG into pixels.
- **Inkscape and ImageMagick:** use Inkscape to open the SVG, press Shift+Ctrl+E and choose an export area, set the width in pixels, name the file and click Export for a PNG. Then run `magick artwork.png artwork.tga`.

### Problems with SVG files

- **Lettering changed:** text layout depends on the fonts available, so a substitute for a missing one alters the drawing.
- **A picture is missing:** artwork that the SVG only points to stays blank on this page; put the image inside the file.
- **The texture looks soft:** bitmaps embedded in the SVG retain their original resolution when enlarged.

guide.title: SVG to TIF: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

The W3C's SVG format uses XML to describe flat graphics through shapes, text and embedded pictures. Stored as instructions, those shapes can be rendered large or small with no loss in sharpness. The format is readable text that CSS and JavaScript can style, and every major browser can display it. Pictures embedded in the file are the exception: they keep their original pixel resolution when enlarged.

### Programs that open SVG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Inkscape edits SVG natively.
- **Windows, Mac, Linux and Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays SVG.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays SVG.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays SVG.

### SVG and TIF compared

TIFF wraps raster data in tags, and Aldus and Microsoft were behind its development. The 6.0 revision dates from 1992, and today the specification belongs to Adobe. One format sits behind both file endings, and its media type is image/tiff. Inside, the choice of compression and color representation varies from file to file, several images can share one file, and archivists rely on it for high-bit-depth imaging and preservation masters. An SVG converted to TIF becomes one raster picture at a fixed size, and its shapes are no longer editable.

On this page the browser paints the SVG at the dimensions it reports, then ImageMagick writes the TIF from those pixels. They pass through at 8 bits per channel, so the TIF is not a high-depth file, and metadata is dropped. The browser loads nothing from outside the SVG, so the result shows embedded data plus fonts installed on your device.

### Other ways to convert SVG to TIF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -density 180 illustration.svg illustration.tif`. A higher -density value gives a larger canvas when ImageMagick reads the SVG.
- **Inkscape and ImageMagick:** in Inkscape, open the SVG and press Shift+Ctrl+E to get the Export PNG Image dialog. Export a PNG at the pixel width you want, then run `magick illustration.png illustration.tif`.

### Problems with SVG files

- **A font was swapped:** the lettering follows whichever fonts your device has, so the drawing changes when one is missing.
- **A picture went missing:** an outside image the SVG points to is not drawn here; put the picture into the file itself.
- **A photo in the drawing looks soft:** a bitmap inside the SVG stays at its own pixel resolution however far you enlarge it.

faqs.question: Can I convert WAV to AMR on this page?
faqs.answer: No. The FFmpeg inside this page has no libopencore_amrnb encoder, which the AMR command asks for, so the run ends with an FFmpeg error.

faqs.question: What error does the page show?
faqs.answer: The run fails with "FFmpeg failed with exit code 1", and FFmpeg's log reports an unknown encoder, libopencore_amrnb.

faqs.question: What does the page ask FFmpeg for?

faqs.question: Is AMR good for music?
faqs.answer: The standard behind AMR was written for GSM speech, so voice is its job rather than music.

faqs.question: How does AMR differ from AMR-WB?
faqs.answer: AMR-WB works at a 16 kHz sampling rate. The two keep different storage signatures, so no extension change turns one into the other.

faqs.question: Will a stereo WAV stay stereo in an AMR?
faqs.answer: No. FFmpeg's libopencore-amrnb encoder is mono-only, and narrowband AMR is sampled at 8 kHz.

faqs.question: Is my WAV uploaded when I try?
faqs.answer: No. No. The conversion attempt runs inside your browser, and the file you chose is left untouched.

guide.title: WAV to AMR: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

A WAV does not name one audio encoding; it is a RIFF-based container for sound. Microsoft and IBM wrote the format down in a multimedia specification dated August 1991. Most files carry linear PCM, although a compressed encoding can sit inside as well. Expect the .wav ending, with audio/wav and audio/x-wav as the usual media-type labels. For production and preservation work there is the Broadcast WAVE extension, which adds metadata, and the Library of Congress recommends WAVE when building digital audio collections.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings in most WAV recordings, PCM variants included.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, because FFmpeg has a demuxer for this format.
- **Web:** Firefox plays WAV directly in the browser.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android, a free media player.

### WAV and AMR compared

Adaptive Multi-Rate is what AMR stands for. ETSI standardized it to carry GSM speech, after which 3GPP chose it for third-generation cellular networks. In the narrowband codec, speech is sampled at 8 kHz and coded in 20-millisecond frames, with eight modes running from 4.75 up to 12.2 kbps. The separate AMR-WB codec samples at 16 kHz, so a narrowband recording cannot supply AMR-WB's wider frequency range. The two also keep different storage signatures. RFC 4867 covers storage files, and audio/AMR is the narrowband media type.

No AMR file comes out of this page. The FFmpeg command it runs requests the libopencore_amrnb encoder, the FFmpeg inside the browser lacks that encoder, and the attempt ends in an unknown encoder error.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AMR

- **Switch Sound File Converter:** select the WAV with Add, set the Output Format field to amr and press Convert. Its supported-formats list names wav as an input and amr as an output.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A WAV that won't open:** recorders sometimes put proprietary compression inside the WAV, and for importing those Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library.
- **Very large recordings:** the original RIFF size fields can fall short, and RF64 takes over.
- **Tags vary by program:** standard INFO chunks hold different information from Broadcast WAVE extensions.

guide.title: WEBP to WEBP: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP image file?

WebP is Google's open-source image format, announced on 30 September 2010. Its lossy mode borrows from the VP8 video codec: still pictures are compressed the way VP8 compresses key frames. The lossless mode is a different design built on LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache. Inside a RIFF container, both modes can carry transparency and animation. Metadata such as an ICC profile, Exif and XMP can ride along.

### Programs that open WebP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP, which has imported and exported WebP natively since 2.10.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads WebP.
- **Windows:** Microsoft's WebP Image Extension lets File Explorer and Photos open WebP images.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays WebP.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays WebP.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays WebP.

### WebP and WebP compared

With the same format on both sides, the file is still decoded and then encoded from scratch. Your browser reads the WebP and a canvas writes the new one, or ImageMagick does where the canvas can't produce WebP. Transparency stays. An animated file keeps only its first frame, and EXIF, ICC and XMP data are left behind. Pixels move through at 8 bits per channel. No quality value is passed along.

That makes it useful for turning an animation into a still or for stripping metadata from a file you plan to publish. For a lossless rewrite or a quality of your own, use a desktop tool.

### Other ways to convert WebP to WebP

- **cwebp:** run `cwebp -lossless -exact still.webp -o recoded.webp`. cwebp accepts WebP input if the file is static, and -exact preserves RGB values in transparent areas.
- **GIMP:** load the WebP through File > Open, pick File > Export As, give it a different name ending in .webp and click Export. In the WebP dialog you will find Lossless, Image quality, Alpha quality, Save animation and the metadata switches Save Exif data, Save XMP data and Save color profile.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick still.webp -define webp:lossless=true rewritten.webp` to encode the new file without any quality loss.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Older browsers:** some versions show a still WebP but have no animation support.
- **Too large:** WebP stops at 16,383 pixels along either axis, so a bigger picture can't be stored.
- **ImageMagick without WebP:** ImageMagick needs the WEBP delegate library to read WebP.

guide.title: WMA to AIFF: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMA file?

Windows Media Audio is the name of four codecs: standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice. Microsoft's ASF container holds their data, and a .wma extension tells you the file is audio alone, not other ASF content. The media type usually associated with it is audio/x-ms-wma. Delivery workflows are one use and intermediate audio storage another, and WMA 9 can encode at a variable bit rate. The extension never tells you which of the four codecs is inside.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player names ASF/WMA among its inputs, with a number of WMA decoders.
- Audacity brings in unprotected WMA only after its optional FFmpeg library has been added.
- FFmpeg decodes WMA 1, WMA 2, Pro, Voice and Lossless in its support matrix.

### WMA and AIFF compared

AIFF is Apple's creation, a wrapper for audio that descends from the IFF family of Electronic Arts. Most often it stores linear PCM without compression; the AIFF-C variant adds compressed audio. Chunks with names exist for the author, a copyright line and annotations. Pro audio users keep masters and intermediate recordings in it, and audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff are common media types.

Here, FFmpeg works in your browser tab and writes audio-only 16-bit big-endian PCM. PCM can't bring back detail a lossy encoder discarded, and it takes more storage than a compressed copy, so a standard WMA becomes an AIFF that is larger but not better. Before converting, check whether your WMA is the Lossless variant, which keeps all its detail, and whether it is copy-protected. Afterwards, play the AIFF from start to end and compare its length with the original.

### Other ways to convert WMA to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.wma -vn -c:a pcm_s16be take.aiff`. The `.aiff` name selects the AIFF format, `-vn` leaves out video and `pcm_s16be` writes 16-bit big-endian samples.
- **Switch Sound File Converter:** click Add and choose the WMA, open the Output Format field and select AIFF, then click Convert.

### Problems with WMA files

- **Protected files:** copy-protected WMA can't be imported through Audacity's FFmpeg library.
- **Audacity offers no WMA import:** WMA import may be missing until the optional FFmpeg component is installed.
- **One WMA opens and another doesn't:** a program may support one WMA codec but lack another, and the extension does not identify the variant.
- **Adobe Audition:** WMA import works on Windows only, with DLMS Format Support enabled.

guide.title: WMV to MKV: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMV file?

Inside a .wmv file, Windows Media coded content sits in Microsoft's ASF container. The ASF design aims at synchronized media storage and network delivery, with room for both audio and video streams. Three generations of Windows Media Video compression, numbered 7, 8 and 9, can encode the picture. The Library of Congress records video/x-ms-wmv as a commonly used media type, rather than an IANA registration.

### Programs that open WMV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC is a desktop player that reads ASF/WMV files and handles the first, second and ninth Windows Media Video codecs.
- FFplay, bundled with the FFmpeg project, uses its decoders for WMV.

### WMV and MKV compared

Matroska, a container for sound and pictures, rests on EBML (a binary form descended from XML) and grew out of the older MCF project. A single file holds more than one video or audio stream, and the design includes chapter marks and descriptive tags. It prescribes no single compression method or fixed level of quality, and IANA registers video/matroska for it.

Nothing here is a plain rewrap. The in-browser FFmpeg builds a new video track with libx264 (ultrafast preset, CRF 32) and a new AAC audio track at 96 kbit/s. A picture whose longer edge passes 1920 pixels is shrunk to fit, a smaller picture stays as it is, and each dimension is rounded down to an even value, which trims one pixel from an odd edge. Frame rates above 30 per second lose frames without changing the duration, while a slower video keeps its rate. Footage marked interlaced goes through a deinterlacing filter. FFmpeg's defaults choose the streams and copy the global tags to the MKV where it can hold them. Before converting, note the source's frame size and rate; afterwards, play the MKV and compare picture, sound and length with the WMV.

### Other ways to convert WMV to MKV

- **FFmpeg stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i footage.wmv -map 0 -c copy wrapped.mkv` to move the existing streams into Matroska without re-encoding.
- **Prism for Windows:** click Add File(s) and pick the WMV, select MKV in the Output Format field, then click Convert.

### Problems with WMV files

- **Decoder gaps:** FFmpeg's own support table marks its decoder for version 9 as only partly working.
- **The container reads but the video won't:** a program that can parse ASF may still lack the codec for the video inside, because the two abilities are independent.
- **Quality varies:** how good the picture looks comes from the codec and its compression settings, and the file extension doesn't reveal either.
